title: Iterative attrs-based hydrator for low-memory streaming response parsing
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Background: Large streaming LLM responses (long chats, incremental tool outputs) can blow up memory when we eagerly materialize pydantic/dataclass objects for every chunk. Goal: implement an alternative lightweight hydrator built on attrs that parses and validates fields incrementally, supports checkpointing across retries, and exposes a backpressure-friendly async iterator compatible with the existing SDK streaming surface.

Scope: prototype attrs-based models + incremental parser, hydration API shim to plug into python-sdk streaming helpers, small benchmark harness, migration guidance for consumer code, and integration tests for retry semantics and schema evolution. This ticket focuses on the core hydrator + adapter (not on full docs or extensive migrations).
acceptance_criteria: 1) attrs-hydrator available behind a feature flag in python-sdk; 2) Streaming iterator yields hydrated partial objects (field-level availability) without retaining full token buffers; 3) Memory for a 10k-token stream reduced >= 4x vs current dataclass-based hydrator in benchmark; 4) Retry after transient error resumes from last checkpoint without rehydrating already-acknowledged fields; 5) API surface passes existing integration tests and is backwards-compatible via an adapter shim.
progress: Prototype implemented (prototype branch attrs-hydrator-v0). Basic iterator and attrs schemas wired into stream surface. Benchmark harness completed with initial numbers showing ~4.6x memory reduction on peak RSS for long-stream test. Edge cases around union fields deferred to follow-up.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Anya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes posted, agreed to use attrs for minimal footprint and to implement a field-available callback for consumer-level optimistic processing.
2025-02-18 - Miguel Alvarez: Prototype of incremental parser landed on branch attrs-hydrator-v0. Parser exposes on_field_ready(name, value) hook and a checkpoint() API for durable offsets.

2025-02-22 - Luke Chen (review): Reviewed parser; recommended deferring heavy validation to a post-checkpoint phase to avoid blocking the stream consumer. Suggested adding a compatibility shim to return legacy dataclass instances lazily.
2025-02-25 - QA: Ran long-stream benchmark (10k tokens) across three runs. Mean peak RSS: dataclass-hydrator 420MB, attrs-hydrator 89MB. Noted higher CPU due to parsing overhead; profiling scheduled.
2025-03-01 - Miguel Alvarez: Opened PR #1824 with basic tests. Failing test around union resolution when a union-tag arrives after fields — added a regression test and marked as TODO.

2025-03-03 - Anya Patel: Decided to ship behind feature flag 'attrs_hydrator=true' and gate default on current dataclass/pydantic path until union semantics are robust. Added follow-up ENG-957212 for union resolution and ENG-957213 for docs/migration guide.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for incremental parser with field-level arrival ordering and checkpoint semantics. 2) Integration tests: simulate transient network failure at token offsets and assert resume checkpoint and no double-emission of fields. 3) Performance tests: long-stream throughput and memory profiles compared to baseline. 4) Contract tests: adapter returns legacy dataclass objects when shim enabled.
rollout_plan: Alpha behind feature flag to internal customers (console teams) + telemetry on memory/latency; monitor for 2 weeks. If stable, expose beta to broader SDK users and add migration docs. Offer opt-in example in quickstart. Full default flip only after union resolution ticket closed.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Consumers expect fully-validated pydantic models immediately; mitigation: provide adapter that performs deferred validation and clear docs on validation semantics. Risk: Increased CPU overhead; mitigation: micro-optimization of parser and optional C-accelerated tokenizer path. Risk: Schema evolution/union tags ordering; mitigation: explicit backstop tests and follow-up ticket for union heuristics.
next_steps: 1) Fix union-resolution regression (ENG-957212). 2) Add low-level C extension for hot path parsing if CPU cost persists. 3) Prepare migration guide and cookbook examples for iteratively-processing generated tool outputs.
